whyWrong.français: That's the masculine form; Marie is a woman — française.
whyWrong.françaises: That's the feminine plural; Marie is one person — française.
whyWrong.France: France is the country; the nationality is française.

whyWrong.françaises: That's the feminine plural; a mixed group (Pierre et Marie) takes masculine français.
whyWrong.française: That's the feminine singular; two people need the plural français.
whyWrong.francs: francs is the old currency / means 'frank', not the nationality français.

whyWrong.français: That's the masculine form; two women take the feminine plural françaises.
whyWrong.française: That's the singular; two people need the plural françaises.

whyWrong.anglais: That's the masculine form; Emma is a woman — anglaise.
whyWrong.anglaises: That's the plural; Emma is one person — anglaise.
whyWrong.angleterre: Angleterre is the country 'England'; the nationality is anglaise.

whyWrong.singapourien: That's the masculine form; Léa is a woman — singapourienne.
whyWrong.singapouriens: That's the masculine plural; Léa is one person — singapourienne.
whyWrong.singapouriennes: That's the feminine plural; Léa is one person — singapourienne.

whyWrong.singapourienne: That's the feminine form; Jun is a man — singapourien.
whyWrong.singapouriens: That's the plural; Jun is one person — singapourien.

items.fullSentence: Anna, Lukas et Felix sont allemands.
items.sentenceTrans: Anna, Lukas and Felix are German.

whyWrong.allemande: That's the feminine singular; the group is plural — allemands.
whyWrong.allemandes: That's the feminine plural; a mixed group takes masculine allemands.
whyWrong.allemand: That's the singular; three people need the plural allemands.

whyWrong.grec: That's the masculine form; Sofia is a woman — grecque.
whyWrong.grecques: That's the feminine plural; Sofia is one person — grecque.
whyWrong.grecs: That's the masculine plural; one woman is grecque.
